children.value: > Fact From Story: Fortnite maker Epic Games is still set to go to trial with the tech giant today, November 6, in hopes of convincing a jury that Google engages in anticompetitive behavior with regard to its Android app store, Google Play, and its commission structure.

> > Fact From Story: Epic argues that Google makes it so difficult for developers and users to get around its Android app store, and that app store’s standard fees, that it’s created an illegal monopoly that unjustly enriches Google while artificially driving up app prices because other stores can’t compete.
> > Fact From Story: Epic wants to break up Google’s alleged monopoly on Android app stores and payment methods, so developers aren’t stuck paying the “Google Tax” or passing that fee along to you.
> > > Fact From Story: Google requires apps to use its own first-party billing system, and charges app developers a 15% to 30% commission on the sales it processes.
> > > Fact From Story: Epic claims that Google has illegal monopolies in “Android app distribution” and “Android in-app payment processing.”
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Companies generally dislike paying high fees or commissions to third parties.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Monopolies are generally considered harmful to consumers because they can lead to higher prices and less innovation.
> Commonsense Knowledge: An antitrust battle is a legal dispute between companies about whether certain business practices are anticompetitive.
